summary: Static keyword co-occurrence in @solana-labs/web3.js bundle without traced-code corroboration
details: Pattern matches fired on the minified CommonJS and ESM bundles of @solana-labs/web3.js, citing co-occurrence of `require('child_process')`, `fetch(`, `POST`, `curl`, and `ping` strings within the same large bundled file. The package is a widely-used Solana JavaScript SDK; bundles of this scope routinely contain `fetch` calls to user-configured RPC endpoints, build-tooling references to `child_process`, and incidental string literals like `curl`/`ping` (e.g., in error messages, agent strings, or vendored libraries). The flagged URLs and POST sites are consistent with the SDK's public RPC client API surface (caller-supplied endpoint URLs), not hardcoded attacker C2. There are no install-time lifecycle hooks invoking these paths and no evidence of credential paths (`~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.npmrc`), browser profile reads, env-var scraping, or known-bad infrastructure. Semantic re-verification of intent in the minified bundle was not completed, so routing to human review rather than allowing outright.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
